source.text: וּפְלִשְׁתִּים֙ לָֽקְח֔וּ אֵ֖ת אֲר֣וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיְבִאֻ֛הוּ מֵאֶ֥בֶן הָעֵ֖זֶר אַשְׁדּֽוֹדָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] Philistines took the ark of God, and brought it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.

en.L: And the Philistines had taken the ark of God, and they brought it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.
en.B: Now the Philistines had captured the ark of God, and they brought it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.
en.R: The Philistines had captured the ark of God, the sacred chest. They carried it from Ebenezer to their city of Ashdod.

es.L: Y los filisteos habían tomado el arca de Dios, y la llevaron de Ebenezer a Asdod.
es.B: Los filisteos habían capturado el arca de Dios, y la llevaron de Ebenezer a Asdod.
es.R: Los filisteos habían capturado el arca de Dios, el cofre sagrado. La llevaron de Ebenezer a Asdod, una de sus ciudades.

fr.L: Et les Philistins avaient pris l’arche de Dieu, et ils l’emmenèrent d’Eben-Ézer à Ashdod.
fr.B: Les Philistins, qui s’étaient emparés de l’arche de Dieu, l’emportèrent d’Eben-Ézer à Ashdod.
fr.R: Les Philistins avaient pris l’arche de Dieu, le coffre sacré. Ils l’ont emportée d’Eben-Ézer jusqu’à leur ville d’Ashdod.

sw.L: Na Wafilisti walikuwa wamelitwaa sanduku la Mungu, wakalileta kutoka Ebenezeri mpaka Ashdodi.
sw.B: Basi Wafilisti walikuwa wameliteka sanduku la Mungu, wakalipeleka kutoka Ebenezeri mpaka Ashdodi.
sw.R: Wafilisti walikuwa wameliteka sanduku la Mungu, lile sanduku takatifu. Wakalibeba kutoka Ebenezeri mpaka mji wao wa Ashdodi.

vi.L: Người Phi-li-tin đã lấy hòm của Đức Chúa Trời và đem nó từ Ê-bên-Ê-xe đến Ách-đốt.
vi.B: Người Phi-li-tin đã cướp được hòm của Đức Chúa Trời, và họ đem hòm từ Ê-bên-Ê-xe đến Ách-đốt.
vi.R: Người Phi-li-tin đã cướp được hòm của Đức Chúa Trời, là chiếc hòm thánh. Họ khiêng hòm từ Ê-bên-Ê-xe về thành Ách-đốt của họ.

decisions.choice: had taken: the story picks up again from the battle of 4:11
decisions.reason: The sentence puts the Philistines first, before the verb. This marks a new start that looks back: after the account of Eli's death and the birth of Ichabod (4:12-22), the narrator returns to the capture of the ark told in 4:11 and follows the ark itself.

decisions.choice: the ark of God: the chest that held the covenant tablets and stood for God's presence
decisions.reason: The ark was the gold-covered chest made at Sinai, with the cherubim on its lid (Exodus 25:10-22). Israel had carried it into battle as if it guaranteed victory (4:3-4), and lost it. This chapter shows that the God of the ark was not captured with it.

decisions.choice: from Ebenezer to Ashdod: from Israel's battle camp to a Philistine city
decisions.reason: Ebenezer was where Israel camped before the battle (4:1). Ashdod was one of the five chief cities of the Philistines, near the coast (Joshua 13:3; 6:17 in this book).

decisions.choice: the sacred chest; their city of Ashdod
decisions.reason: Readable explains once what the ark was and that Ashdod was a Philistine city, so that young readers can follow the story.

decisions.choice: Ashdodi; Gathi, Ekroni (verses 8, 10)
decisions.reason: The Philistine cities take the Swahili forms of the terms note.

decisions.choice: "Ách-đốt", and "Gát", "Éc-rôn" (verses 8, 10)
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note for the Philistine cities.

source.text: וַיִּקְח֤וּ פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ אֶת־אֲר֣וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיָּבִ֥יאוּ אֹת֖וֹ בֵּ֣ית דָּג֑וֹן וַיַּצִּ֥יגוּ אֹת֖וֹ אֵ֥צֶל דָּגֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And took [the] Philistines the ark of God and brought it [into the] house of Dagon, and set it beside Dagon.

en.L: And the Philistines took the ark of God and brought it into the house of Dagon, and set it beside Dagon.
en.B: The Philistines took the ark of God, brought it into the temple of Dagon, and set it up beside Dagon.
en.R: They carried the ark of God into the temple of their god Dagon and set it up next to his statue.

es.L: Y los filisteos tomaron el arca de Dios y la metieron en la casa de Dagón, y la colocaron junto a Dagón.
es.B: Los filisteos tomaron el arca de Dios, la llevaron al templo de Dagón y la colocaron junto a Dagón.
es.R: Llevaron el arca de Dios al templo de Dagón, su dios, y la pusieron junto a su estatua.

fr.L: Et les Philistins prirent l’arche de Dieu et l’amenèrent dans la maison de Dagon, et ils la placèrent à côté de Dagon.
fr.B: Les Philistins prirent l’arche de Dieu, la firent entrer dans le temple de Dagon et l’installèrent à côté de Dagon.
fr.R: Ils ont porté l’arche de Dieu dans le temple de leur dieu Dagon et l’ont installée à côté de sa statue.

sw.L: Na Wafilisti wakalitwaa sanduku la Mungu wakaliingiza nyumbani mwa Dagoni, wakaliweka kando ya Dagoni.
sw.B: Wafilisti walilichukua sanduku la Mungu, wakaliingiza katika hekalu la Dagoni, wakaliweka kando ya Dagoni.
sw.R: Walilibeba sanduku la Mungu wakaliingiza katika hekalu la mungu wao Dagoni, wakaliweka karibu na sanamu yake.

vi.L: Người Phi-li-tin lấy hòm của Đức Chúa Trời, đem vào nhà của Đa-gôn và đặt bên cạnh Đa-gôn.
vi.B: Người Phi-li-tin lấy hòm của Đức Chúa Trời, đem vào đền thờ Đa-gôn và đặt bên cạnh Đa-gôn.
vi.R: Họ khiêng hòm của Đức Chúa Trời vào đền thờ thần Đa-gôn của họ và đặt cạnh tượng thần ấy.

decisions.choice: Dagon: a god the Philistines worshiped
decisions.reason: Dagon had a temple at Gaza as well (Judges 16:23-30). He was worshiped in the region long before the Philistines came, and his name sounds like a common word for grain. Beside Dagon means beside his image in the temple.

decisions.choice: house of Dagon: Dagon's temple
decisions.reason: "House" is the usual word for a god's temple, as with the house of the LORD at Shiloh (1:7, 24).

decisions.choice: setting the ark beside Dagon: a trophy brought before the winning god
decisions.reason: Conquerors often carried the images of defeated peoples into the temple of their own god, to show that their god had won. The Philistines treat the ark this way. The next two mornings show which God is stronger.

decisions.choice: temple (Balanced and Readable); his statue (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "temple" for the house of a god. Readable says "statue" where the Hebrew names Dagon himself, since the ark stood beside his image.

decisions.choice: "Dagón"; "Asdod", "Gat", "Ecrón"
decisions.reason: For 1 and 2 Samuel: the god and the Philistine cities in their usual Spanish forms, as the Samuel terms note gives Gat, Ecrón and Asdod.

decisions.choice: Dagoni; mungu wao
decisions.reason: The name takes a Swahili ending; a false god is "mungu" in lower case, as in the published Pentateuch.

decisions.choice: "Đa-gôn"; "thần Đa-gôn" at Readable
decisions.reason: The usual Vietnamese form of the name; Readable says he was a god, as the English Readable does with "their god Dagon".

source.text: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֤מוּ אַשְׁדּוֹדִים֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וְהִנֵּ֣ה דָג֗וֹן נֹפֵ֤ל לְפָנָיו֙ אַ֔רְצָה לִפְנֵ֖י אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּקְחוּ֙ אֶת־דָּג֔וֹן וַיָּשִׁ֥בוּ אֹת֖וֹ לִמְקוֹמֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And rose early [the] Ashdodites on [the] next day, and look, Dagon [was] fallen on his face to [the] ground before [the] ark of YHWH; and they took Dagon and returned him to his place.

en.L: And the Ashdodites rose early the next day, and look, Dagon had fallen on his face to the ground before the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And they took Dagon and put him back in his place.
en.B: When the people of Ashdod got up early the next day, there was Dagon, fallen face down on the ground before the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. So they took Dagon and set him back in his place.
en.R: Early the next morning the people of Ashdod found Dagon lying face down on the ground in front of the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They picked Dagon up and put him back where he belonged.

es.L: Y los de Asdod se levantaron temprano al día siguiente, y he aquí, Dagón había caído sobre su rostro en tierra delante del arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Y tomaron a Dagón y lo volvieron a su lugar.
es.B: Cuando los de Asdod se levantaron temprano al día siguiente, allí estaba Dagón, caído boca abajo en el suelo delante del arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Así que tomaron a Dagón y lo volvieron a poner en su sitio.
es.R: A la mañana siguiente, muy temprano, la gente de Asdod encontró a Dagón tirado boca abajo en el suelo, delante del arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Levantaron a Dagón y lo pusieron otra vez en su lugar.

fr.L: Et les Ashdodiens se levèrent de bon matin le lendemain, et voici, Dagon était tombé sur sa face, à terre, devant l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Et ils prirent Dagon et le remirent à sa place.
fr.B: Quand les habitants d’Ashdod se levèrent tôt le lendemain, Dagon était là, tombé face contre terre devant l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Ils prirent donc Dagon et le remirent à sa place.
fr.R: Le lendemain, très tôt, les habitants d’Ashdod ont trouvé Dagon couché face contre terre devant l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Ils ont relevé Dagon et l’ont remis à sa place.

sw.L: Na Waashdodi wakaamka mapema siku iliyofuata, na tazama, Dagoni alikuwa ameanguka kifudifudi chini mbele ya sanduku la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Nao wakamchukua Dagoni wakamrudisha mahali pake.
sw.B: Watu wa Ashdodi walipoamka mapema siku iliyofuata, kumbe Dagoni alikuwa ameanguka kifudifudi chini mbele ya sanduku la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Basi wakamchukua Dagoni wakamrudisha mahali pake.
sw.R: Asubuhi na mapema siku iliyofuata watu wa Ashdodi walimkuta Dagoni amelala kifudifudi chini mbele ya sanduku la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Wakamwinua Dagoni wakamrudisha mahali pake.

vi.L: Hôm sau người Ách-đốt dậy sớm, và kìa, Đa-gôn đã ngã sấp mặt xuống đất trước hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Họ lấy Đa-gôn và đặt lại chỗ cũ.
vi.B: Sáng hôm sau, khi người Ách-đốt dậy sớm, thì thấy Đa-gôn ngã sấp mặt xuống đất trước hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Vậy họ lấy Đa-gôn dựng lại chỗ cũ.
vi.R: Sáng sớm hôm sau, người Ách-đốt thấy tượng Đa-gôn nằm sấp mặt dưới đất trước hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Họ đỡ Đa-gôn lên và đặt lại chỗ cũ.

decisions.choice: fallen on his face before the ark: the posture of a worshiper or a defeated servant
decisions.reason: Falling face down to the ground is how a person bows before a greater lord (Joshua 5:14; 1 Samuel 25:23). The god of the winning army lies before the ark of the God whose people lost. The narrator now names the ark "the ark of the LORD", using the divine name as the LORD acts.

decisions.choice: look: what the people of Ashdod saw as they came in
decisions.reason: The word draws the reader into the moment of discovery, seeing the fallen image through the eyes of the people who found it.

decisions.choice: they took Dagon and put him back: the god had to be set up by human hands
decisions.reason: The image could not raise itself. The point is made with a quiet irony that the prophets later make openly (Isaiah 46:7).

decisions.choice: look (Literal); there was (Balanced); found (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the pointing word as "look". Balanced says "there was Dagon", and Readable turns it into the verb "found", which carries the same surprise in plain English.

source.text: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣מוּ בַבֹּקֶר֮ מִֽמָּחֳרָת֒ וְהִנֵּ֣ה דָג֗וֹן נֹפֵ֤ל לְפָנָיו֙ אַ֔רְצָה לִפְנֵ֖י אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֑ה וְרֹ֨אשׁ דָּג֜וֹן וּשְׁתֵּ֣י׀כַּפּ֣וֹת יָדָ֗יו כְּרֻתוֹת֙ אֶל־הַמִּפְתָּ֔ן רַ֥ק דָּג֖וֹן נִשְׁאַ֥ר עָלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And they rose early in [the] morning on [the] next day, and look, Dagon [was] fallen on his face to [the] ground before [the] ark of YHWH, and [the] head of Dagon and [the] two palms of his hands [were] cut off on the threshold; only Dagon was left on him.

en.L: And they rose early in the morning the next day, and look, Dagon had fallen on his face to the ground before the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the head of Dagon and both palms of his hands [were] cut off [and lying] on the threshold. Only Dagon was left of him.
en.B: Early the following morning they rose, and there was Dagon, fallen face down on the ground before the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Dagon's head and both his hands lay cut off on the threshold; only his body was left.
en.R: The next morning they got up early again, and Dagon had fallen face down on the ground in front of the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} once more. This time his head and both his hands had been cut off. They were lying on the threshold of the doorway. Only his body was left.

es.L: Y se levantaron temprano por la mañana al día siguiente, y he aquí, Dagón había caído sobre su rostro en tierra delante del arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y la cabeza de Dagón y las dos palmas de sus manos [estaban] cortadas [y tiradas] sobre el umbral. Solo Dagón le había quedado.
es.B: A la mañana siguiente se levantaron temprano, y allí estaba Dagón, caído boca abajo en el suelo delante del arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. La cabeza de Dagón y sus dos manos estaban cortadas sobre el umbral; solo le quedaba el tronco.
es.R: A la mañana siguiente volvieron a levantarse temprano, y otra vez Dagón estaba caído boca abajo en el suelo, delante del arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Esta vez le habían cortado la cabeza y las dos manos. Estaban tiradas sobre el umbral de la puerta. Solo quedaba el tronco.

fr.L: Et ils se levèrent de bon matin le lendemain, et voici, Dagon était tombé sur sa face, à terre, devant l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ; et la tête de Dagon et les deux paumes de ses mains [étaient] coupées, [gisant] sur le seuil. Seul Dagon lui restait.
fr.B: Le lendemain, ils se levèrent de bon matin, et Dagon était là, tombé face contre terre devant l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. La tête de Dagon et ses deux mains, coupées, gisaient sur le seuil ; il ne restait que son tronc.
fr.R: Le lendemain matin, ils se sont encore levés tôt, et Dagon était de nouveau tombé face contre terre devant l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Cette fois, sa tête et ses deux mains avaient été coupées. Elles étaient par terre, sur le seuil de la porte. Il ne restait que son corps.

sw.L: Nao wakaamka asubuhi na mapema siku iliyofuata, na tazama, Dagoni alikuwa ameanguka kifudifudi chini mbele ya sanduku la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, na kichwa cha Dagoni na viganja vyote viwili vya mikono yake [vilikuwa] vimekatwa [vikiwa] kizingitini. Dagoni tu [kiwiliwili] kilibaki kwake.
sw.B: Asubuhi na mapema siku iliyofuata waliamka, na kumbe Dagoni alikuwa ameanguka kifudifudi chini mbele ya sanduku la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Kichwa cha Dagoni na mikono yake yote miwili vilikuwa vimekatwa vikiwa kizingitini; kiwiliwili chake tu ndicho kilichobaki.
sw.R: Asubuhi iliyofuata waliamka mapema tena, na Dagoni alikuwa ameanguka kifudifudi tena chini mbele ya sanduku la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Safari hii kichwa chake na mikono yake yote miwili vilikuwa vimekatwa. Vilikuwa vimelala kwenye kizingiti cha mlango. Kiwiliwili chake tu ndicho kilichobaki.

vi.L: Sáng hôm sau nữa họ dậy sớm, và kìa, Đa-gôn đã ngã sấp mặt xuống đất trước hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, đầu của Đa-gôn và hai bàn tay nó bị chặt đứt [nằm] trên ngưỡng cửa. Chỉ còn lại Đa-gôn trên nó.
vi.B: Sáng sớm hôm sau nữa họ dậy, thì kìa, Đa-gôn lại ngã sấp mặt xuống đất trước hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Đầu và hai bàn tay của Đa-gôn bị chặt đứt nằm trên ngưỡng cửa; chỉ còn lại thân mình.
vi.R: Sáng hôm sau họ lại dậy sớm, và một lần nữa tượng Đa-gôn ngã sấp mặt dưới đất trước hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Lần này đầu và hai bàn tay của tượng đã bị chặt đứt. Chúng nằm trên ngưỡng cửa. Chỉ còn lại thân tượng.

decisions.choice: head and hands cut off: the marks of an enemy beaten in battle
decisions.reason: Victors cut off the heads or hands of defeated enemies (Judges 8:6; 1 Samuel 17:51; 31:9). Dagon is shown not only bowing but lying like a slain enemy before the ark.

decisions.choice: only Dagon was left: only the trunk of the image remained
alternatives: only Dagon's trunk was left to him
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says, briefly, "only Dagon was left on him". The sense is clear enough: the head and hands were gone and only the body of the statue was left. The wording is unusual, and it may be that a word meaning "body" or "trunk" has dropped out of the text, or that the name stands here for the rest of the figure.

decisions.choice: the threshold: the raised stone at the temple doorway
decisions.reason: The broken pieces lay at the entrance. The next verse explains a custom about this threshold that was still kept when the book was written.

decisions.choice: his body
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what was left, his body, since "only Dagon was left" would not make sense in English after his head and hands are gone.

decisions.choice: again; once more; this time
decisions.reason: Readable adds these small words to show that the same thing happened a second time and was worse, as the repeated wording of verses 3 and 4 shows.

decisions.choice: Dagoni tu [kiwiliwili] kilibaki kwake
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "only Dagon was left on him", meaning the trunk of the image (m2); Swahili cannot leave "Dagon" standing for the trunk without confusion, so Literal supplies "kiwiliwili" in brackets.

source.text: עַל־כֵּ֡ן לֹֽא־יִדְרְכוּ֩ כֹהֲנֵ֨י דָג֜וֹן וְכָֽל־הַבָּאִ֧ים בֵּית־דָּג֛וֹן עַל־מִפְתַּ֥ן דָּג֖וֹן בְּאַשְׁדּ֑וֹד עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Therefore not tread [the] priests of Dagon and all those coming [into the] house of Dagon on [the] threshold of Dagon in Ashdod until this day.

en.L: Therefore the priests of Dagon and all who come into the house of Dagon do not tread on the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod, to this day.
en.B: That is why, to this day, the priests of Dagon and everyone who enters Dagon's temple in Ashdod do not step on Dagon's threshold.
en.R: That is why, to this day, Dagon's priests and everyone who goes into his temple in Ashdod do not step on the threshold.

es.L: Por eso los sacerdotes de Dagón y todos los que entran en la casa de Dagón no pisan el umbral de Dagón en Asdod, hasta el día de hoy.
es.B: Por eso, hasta el día de hoy, los sacerdotes de Dagón y todos los que entran en su templo en Asdod no pisan el umbral de Dagón.
es.R: Por eso, hasta el día de hoy, los sacerdotes de Dagón y todos los que entran en su templo en Asdod no pisan el umbral.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi les prêtres de Dagon et tous ceux qui entrent dans la maison de Dagon ne marchent pas sur le seuil de Dagon à Ashdod, jusqu’à ce jour.
fr.B: Voilà pourquoi, jusqu’à aujourd’hui, les prêtres de Dagon et tous ceux qui entrent dans son temple à Ashdod ne posent pas le pied sur le seuil de Dagon.
fr.R: C’est pour cela que, jusqu’à aujourd’hui, les prêtres de Dagon et tous ceux qui entrent dans son temple à Ashdod ne marchent pas sur le seuil.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo makuhani wa Dagoni na wote wanaoingia nyumbani mwa Dagoni hawakanyagi kizingiti cha Dagoni huko Ashdodi, mpaka leo.
sw.B: Ndiyo sababu, mpaka leo, makuhani wa Dagoni na kila mtu anayeingia katika hekalu la Dagoni huko Ashdodi hawakanyagi kizingiti cha Dagoni.
sw.R: Ndiyo sababu, mpaka leo, makuhani wa Dagoni na kila mtu anayeingia katika hekalu lake huko Ashdodi hawakanyagi kizingiti.

vi.L: Vì vậy các thầy tế lễ của Đa-gôn và mọi người vào nhà Đa-gôn không giẫm lên ngưỡng cửa của Đa-gôn ở Ách-đốt cho đến ngày nay.
vi.B: Vì thế, cho đến ngày nay, các thầy tế lễ của Đa-gôn và mọi người vào đền thờ Đa-gôn ở Ách-đốt đều không bước lên ngưỡng cửa của Đa-gôn.
vi.R: Vì thế cho đến ngày nay, các thầy tế lễ của Đa-gôn và mọi người vào đền thờ thần ấy ở Ách-đốt đều không bước lên ngưỡng cửa.

decisions.choice: they do not tread on the threshold: a custom explained by this event
decisions.reason: People entering stepped over the threshold rather than on it, because the broken image had lain there. Zephaniah 1:9 also speaks of people who leap over the threshold, perhaps a practice of the same kind.

decisions.choice: to this day: up to the time the book was written
decisions.reason: The phrase, used here for the first time in 1 Samuel, refers to the writer's own day, when the custom was still kept (also 6:18).

decisions.choice: do not tread: a lasting habit
decisions.reason: The verb describes what is done again and again, a rule kept every time someone enters.

decisions.choice: temple
decisions.reason: As in verse 2, Balanced and Readable say "temple" for Dagon's house.

decisions.choice: "hasta el día de hoy" at every level
decisions.reason: For 1 and 2 Samuel, as the Samuel terms note: one wording at every level for the writer's own day (m2).

decisions.choice: mpaka leo
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note: "to this day" means the writer's own day; Swahili says "mpaka leo" at every level.

decisions.choice: "cho đến ngày nay" at every level
decisions.reason: The writer's own day (meaning decision), as the Samuel terms note sets for this formula.

source.text: וַתִּכְבַּ֧ד יַד־יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־הָאַשְׁדּוֹדִ֖ים וַיְשִׁמֵּ֑ם וַיַּ֤ךְ אֹתָם֙ בַּטְּחֹרִ֔יםאֶת־אַשְׁדּ֖וֹד וְאֶת־גְּבוּלֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And was heavy [the] hand of YHWH on the Ashdodites, and he devastated them and struck them with tumors, Ashdod and its territories.

en.L: And the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was heavy on the Ashdodites, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} devastated them and struck them with tumors, Ashdod and its territories.
en.B: Then the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} weighed heavily on the people of Ashdod. He brought ruin on them and struck them with tumors, both Ashdod and the land around it.
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} dealt very harshly with the people of Ashdod. He brought disaster on them and struck them with tumors, in the city and in the land around it.

es.L: Y la mano {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} se hizo pesada sobre los de Asdod, y los asoló y los hirió con tumores, a Asdod y sus territorios.
es.B: Entonces la mano {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} cayó con peso sobre la gente de Asdod. Los arruinó y los hirió con tumores, tanto a Asdod como a sus alrededores.
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} castigó con mucha dureza a la gente de Asdod. Les mandó desgracias y los hirió con tumores, en la ciudad y en sus alrededores.

fr.L: Et la main {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} s’appesantit sur les Ashdodiens, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les ravagea et les frappa de tumeurs, Ashdod et son territoire.
fr.B: Alors la main {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} pesa lourdement sur les habitants d’Ashdod. Il les dévasta et les frappa de tumeurs, à Ashdod et dans ses environs.
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a traité très durement les habitants d’Ashdod. Il leur a envoyé le malheur et les a frappés de tumeurs, dans la ville et dans toute la région.

sw.L: Na mkono wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ukawa mzito juu ya Waashdodi, akawaangamiza na kuwapiga kwa majipu, Ashdodi na mipaka yake.
sw.B: Ndipo mkono wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ukawalemea sana watu wa Ashdodi. Akawaletea maangamizi na kuwapiga kwa majipu, Ashdodi na nchi iliyouzunguka.
sw.R: Ndipo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawatendea watu wa Ashdodi kwa ukali mwingi. Akawaletea maafa na kuwapiga kwa majipu, wale wa mjini na wale wa nchi iliyouzunguka.

vi.L: Tay của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đè nặng trên người Ách-đốt; {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} tàn phá họ và giáng bướu trên họ, cả Ách-đốt và các vùng lân cận.
vi.B: Rồi tay của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đè nặng trên người Ách-đốt. Ngài làm cho họ điêu đứng và giáng bướu độc trên họ, cả trong thành Ách-đốt lẫn vùng chung quanh.
vi.R: Rồi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} trừng phạt người Ách-đốt rất nặng. Ngài giáng tai họa trên họ và khiến họ nổi bướu, cả trong thành lẫn vùng chung quanh.

decisions.choice: the hand of the LORD was heavy: the LORD pressed hard on them with his power
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power at work. A heavy hand presses down and punishes. The picture returns in verses 7, 9 and 11, and the Philistines had already feared what this God did to Egypt (4:8).

decisions.choice: devastated them: brought ruin on them
decisions.reason: The verb can mean either to lay waste or to fill with horror. Here it sums up the disaster, which the rest of the verse names.

decisions.choice: tumors: painful swellings, of a kind not known for certain
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) here, in verses 9 and 12 and in 6:4-5 spell *'ofalim*, "swellings" or "mounds", but the scribes marked them to be read aloud as *techorim* (qere), the word used in 6:11 and 6:17. The same pair appears in Deuteronomy 28:27. The reading may have been chosen as a more decent word. Both name a painful lump on the body. Some take them to be hemorrhoids; others take them to be the swellings of a plague, since many people died (verses 11-12) and the Philistines later make gold mice as well as gold tumors (6:4-5). The text does not say which.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew text without the addition in the old Greek translation
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation is longer here: it adds that mice swarmed in the land and there was a great deadly panic in the city. This prepares for the gold mice of 6:4-5, which the Hebrew mentions only there. The Westminster Leningrad Codex, which this translation follows, does not have the addition.

decisions.choice: Ashdod and its territories: the whole area struck, city and surrounding land
decisions.reason: The words follow "them" and spell out who was struck: the city and the villages and fields that belonged to it.

decisions.choice: dealt very harshly with
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of a heavy hand as the LORD dealing harshly with the people.

decisions.choice: majipu
decisions.reason: The swellings are of a kind not known for certain (m3); "majipu", painful swellings or boils, names the affliction without deciding what disease it was, as the English "tumors" does.

decisions.choice: "bướu" (L, R), "bướu độc" (B) for the tumors
decisions.reason: Painful swellings of a kind not known for certain (meaning decision); "bướu" names a swelling without naming a disease.

source.text: וַיִּרְא֥וּ אַנְשֵֽׁי־אַשְׁדּ֖וֹד כִּֽי־כֵ֑ן וְאָמְר֗וּ לֹֽא־יֵשֵׁ֞ב אֲר֨וֹן אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ עִמָּ֔נוּ כִּֽי־קָשְׁתָ֤ה יָדוֹ֙ עָלֵ֔ינוּ וְעַ֖ל דָּג֥וֹן אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw [the] men of Ashdod that [it was] so, and they said, not will stay [the] ark of [the] God of Israel with us, for hard [is] his hand on us and on Dagon our god.

en.L: And the men of Ashdod saw that [it was] so, and they said, "The ark of the God of Israel must not stay with us, for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand is hard on us and on Dagon our god."
en.B: When the {{gender:people|men}} of Ashdod saw how things stood, they said, "The ark of the God of Israel must not remain among us. His hand is pressing hard on us and on Dagon our god."
en.R: The {{gender:people|men}} of Ashdod saw what was happening, and they said, "We cannot keep the ark of the God of Israel here. He is being hard on us and on our god Dagon."

es.L: Y los hombres de Asdod vieron que [era] así, y dijeron: «El arca del Dios de Israel no debe quedarse con nosotros, porque {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano es dura contra nosotros y contra Dagón nuestro dios».
es.B: Cuando los habitantes de Asdod vieron lo que pasaba, dijeron: «El arca del Dios de Israel no puede quedarse entre nosotros. Su mano está cayendo con dureza sobre nosotros y sobre Dagón nuestro dios».
es.R: Los habitantes de Asdod vieron lo que estaba pasando, y dijeron: «No podemos quedarnos aquí con el arca del Dios de Israel. Él nos está tratando con dureza a nosotros y a nuestro dios Dagón».

fr.L: Et les hommes d’Ashdod virent qu’[il en était] ainsi, et ils dirent : « L’arche du Dieu d’Israël ne restera pas avec nous, car {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main est dure contre nous et contre Dagon notre dieu. »
fr.B: Voyant ce qui se passait, {{gender:les gens|les hommes}} d’Ashdod dirent : « L’arche du Dieu d’Israël ne doit pas rester chez nous. Sa main s’abat durement sur nous et sur Dagon notre dieu. »
fr.R: {{gender:Les gens|Les hommes}} d’Ashdod ont vu ce qui se passait, et ils ont dit : « Nous ne pouvons pas garder ici l’arche du Dieu d’Israël. Il est dur avec nous et avec notre dieu Dagon. »

sw.L: Na watu wa Ashdodi wakaona kwamba [ilikuwa] hivyo, wakasema, "Sanduku la Mungu wa Israeli lisikae kwetu, kwa maana mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} ni mgumu juu yetu na juu ya Dagoni mungu wetu."
sw.B: Watu wa Ashdodi walipoona jinsi mambo yalivyokuwa, wakasema, "Sanduku la Mungu wa Israeli lisibaki kwetu. Mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} unatulemea sisi na Dagoni mungu wetu."
sw.R: Watu wa Ashdodi waliona yaliyokuwa yakitokea, wakasema, "Hatuwezi kulibakiza hapa sanduku la Mungu wa Israeli. Anatutendea kwa ukali sisi na mungu wetu Dagoni."

vi.L: Người Ách-đốt thấy [sự việc là] như vậy thì nói: "Hòm của Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên không được ở lại với chúng ta, vì tay {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nặng nề trên chúng ta và trên Đa-gôn, thần của chúng ta."
vi.B: Khi {{gender:dân thành|đàn ông thành}} Ách-đốt thấy sự việc như thế, họ nói: "Hòm của Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên không được ở lại giữa chúng ta. Tay vị thần ấy đang đè nặng trên chúng ta và trên Đa-gôn, thần của chúng ta."
vi.R: {{gender:Dân thành|Đàn ông thành}} Ách-đốt thấy điều đang xảy ra thì nói: "Chúng ta không thể giữ hòm của Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên ở đây. Vị thần ấy đang trừng phạt chúng ta và thần Đa-gôn của chúng ta quá nặng."

decisions.choice: his hand is hard on us and on Dagon our god: the God of Israel is fighting both the people and their god
decisions.reason: The people of Ashdod see that the disease and the fall of their god have one cause. They name the God of Israel as the one acting, against them and against Dagon, as he had acted against the gods of Egypt (Exodus 12:12; 1 Samuel 4:8).

decisions.choice: must not stay: a decision, not only a prediction
decisions.reason: The verb could be read "will not stay", but in their mouths it is a resolve: the ark has to leave.

decisions.choice: hard: severe, harsh
decisions.reason: This word is close in sense to the "heavy" hand of verse 6; both describe a pressure that will not let up.

decisions.choice: people of Ashdod (default); men of Ashdod (alternative)
decisions.reason: "Men of" a city is the usual way of naming its inhabitants, and the disease struck everyone (verse 9), so Balanced and Readable say "people" by default with "men" as the alternative.

decisions.choice: He is being hard on us
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the hand directly.

decisions.choice: {{gender:les gens|les hommes}} d'Ashdod
decisions.reason: As the English, the default says that the townspeople as a whole speak; "les gens" is plainly inclusive in French, where "les habitants" is grammatically masculine. Literal keeps "les hommes", as the English Literal keeps "men".

decisions.choice: "los habitantes de Asdod", with no gender span (L: "los hombres de Asdod")
decisions.reason: The English Balanced and Readable offer "people" or "men" of Ashdod (r-en-1). Spanish "los habitantes" names all the city's people, men and women, in one natural word, so it needs no setting; Literal keeps "los hombres", the Hebrew "men of". The same holds for the other cities in this chapter.

decisions.choice: watu wa Ashdodi, no gender span
alternatives: a span like the English one
decisions.reason: Swahili "watu" covers men and women alike and is the ordinary word here, so the English gender span has no second wording in Swahili; Literal also says "watu", which in Swahili is no narrower than the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: "{{gender:dân thành|đàn ông thành}} Ách-đốt"
decisions.reason: As the English setting; Vietnamese has both wordings. Literal says "người Ách-đốt", which already covers either reading.

decisions.choice: the Philistines speak of Israel's God as "vị thần ấy", with no capital or deity span
decisions.reason: The Vietnamese capital "Ngài" is the believer's reverence; on Philistine lips Vietnamese uses their own word, as for "một vị thần" in 4:7. Literal keeps the pronoun with its span, as the English.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלְח֡וּ וַיַּאַסְפוּ֩ אֶת־כָּל־סַרְנֵ֨י פְלִשְׁתִּ֜ים אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ מַֽה־נַּעֲשֶׂ֗ה לַֽאֲרוֹן֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ גַּ֣ת יִסֹּ֔ב אֲר֖וֹן אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיַּסֵּ֕בּוּ אֶת־אֲר֖וֹן אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they sent and gathered all [the] rulers of [the] Philistines to them, and said, what shall we do with [the] ark of [the] God of Israel? And they said, to Gath let go around [the] ark of [the] God of Israel. And they brought around [the] ark of [the] God of Israel.

en.L: And they sent and gathered all the rulers of the Philistines to themselves, and said, "What shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel?" And they said, "Let the ark of the God of Israel go around to Gath." And they brought the ark of the God of Israel around.
en.B: So they sent for all the rulers of the Philistines and gathered them together. "What should we do with the ark of the God of Israel?" they asked. The rulers replied, "Have the ark of the God of Israel taken over to Gath." So they took the ark of the God of Israel over there.
en.R: So they sent for all the Philistine rulers to meet together and asked them, "What should we do with the ark of the God of Israel?" The rulers said, "Move it to Gath." So the ark of Israel's God was moved to Gath.

es.L: Y enviaron a reunir consigo a todos los jefes de los filisteos, y dijeron: «¿Qué haremos con el arca del Dios de Israel?». Y ellos dijeron: «Que el arca del Dios de Israel pase a Gat». Y pasaron allá el arca del Dios de Israel.
es.B: Así que mandaron llamar a todos los jefes de los filisteos y los reunieron. «¿Qué debemos hacer con el arca del Dios de Israel?», preguntaron. Los jefes respondieron: «Que lleven el arca del Dios de Israel a Gat». Y llevaron allá el arca del Dios de Israel.
es.R: Entonces llamaron a todos los jefes de los filisteos para que se reunieran, y les preguntaron: «¿Qué hacemos con el arca del Dios de Israel?». Los jefes dijeron: «{{plural_you:Llévenla|Llevadla}} a Gat». Así que el arca del Dios de Israel fue llevada a Gat.

fr.L: Et ils envoyèrent rassembler auprès d’eux tous les princes des Philistins, et dirent : « Que ferons-nous de l’arche du Dieu d’Israël ? » Et ils dirent : « Qu’on fasse passer l’arche du Dieu d’Israël à Gath. » Et ils firent passer l’arche du Dieu d’Israël.
fr.B: Ils firent donc venir tous les princes des Philistins et les réunirent. « Que devons-nous faire de l’arche du Dieu d’Israël ? » demandèrent-ils. Les princes répondirent : « Qu’on transporte l’arche du Dieu d’Israël à Gath. » Et l’on y transporta l’arche du Dieu d’Israël.
fr.R: Alors ils ont fait venir tous les princes des Philistins pour une réunion et leur ont demandé : « Que devons-nous faire de l’arche du Dieu d’Israël ? » Les princes ont répondu : « Transportez-la à Gath. » On a donc transporté l’arche du Dieu d’Israël à Gath.

sw.L: Nao wakatuma wakawakusanya kwao wakuu wote wa Wafilisti, wakasema, "Tulifanye nini sanduku la Mungu wa Israeli?" Nao wakasema, "Sanduku la Mungu wa Israeli na lizungushwe mpaka Gathi." Nao wakalizungusha sanduku la Mungu wa Israeli.
sw.B: Basi wakatuma ujumbe kwa wakuu wote wa Wafilisti, wakawakusanya pamoja. Wakauliza, "Tufanye nini na sanduku la Mungu wa Israeli?" Wakuu wakajibu, "Sanduku la Mungu wa Israeli lipelekwe Gathi." Basi wakalipeleka sanduku la Mungu wa Israeli huko.
sw.R: Basi wakawaita wakuu wote wa Wafilisti wakutane pamoja, wakawauliza, "Tufanye nini na sanduku la Mungu wa Israeli?" Wakuu wakasema, "Lipelekeni Gathi." Basi sanduku la Mungu wa Israeli likapelekwa Gathi.

vi.L: Họ sai người đi triệu tập tất cả các lãnh chúa Phi-li-tin đến với mình và nói: "Chúng ta phải làm gì với hòm của Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên?" Họ nói: "Hãy để hòm của Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên đi vòng qua Gát." Vậy họ đem hòm của Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên đi vòng qua đó.
vi.B: Vậy họ sai người mời tất cả các lãnh chúa Phi-li-tin họp lại và hỏi: "Chúng ta phải làm gì với hòm của Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên?" Các lãnh chúa đáp: "Hãy chuyển hòm của Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên sang Gát." Vậy họ chuyển hòm của Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên sang đó.
vi.R: Vậy họ mời tất cả các lãnh chúa Phi-li-tin đến họp và hỏi: "Chúng ta phải làm gì với hòm của Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên?" Các lãnh chúa đáp: "Hãy chuyển hòm sang Gát." Vậy hòm của Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên được chuyển sang Gát.

decisions.choice: the rulers of the Philistines: the lords of the five Philistine cities
decisions.reason: This title is used only for the Philistine leaders. Each of the five cities, Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron, had its own ruler, and they acted together on matters of war and state (Joshua 13:3; 1 Samuel 6:16-18).

decisions.choice: they said: the rulers give the answer
decisions.reason: The Hebrew simply says "they said". Since the question was put to the rulers, the answer is most naturally theirs.

decisions.choice: Gath: another of the five cities, further inland
decisions.reason: Gath lay east of Ashdod, toward the hill country of Judah. It was later the home of Goliath (17:4).

decisions.choice: go around, bring around: move from one place to another
decisions.reason: The verb is used three times in verses 8-10. The ark is passed around from city to city, and the Ekronites use the same word in their complaint (verse 10).

decisions.choice: The rulers replied (Balanced); The rulers said (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speakers, since in English "they said" right after "they asked" would sound like the same people answering themselves.

decisions.choice: "les princes des Philistins"
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note settles: the rulers of the five Philistine cities (m1). "Princes" in older French meant rulers in general, as here; "seigneurs" would clash with "le Seigneur".

decisions.choice: "los jefes de los filisteos" at every level
decisions.reason: For 1 and 2 Samuel, as the Samuel terms note: the rulers of the five Philistine cities (m1) are "jefes", kept apart from "gobernante", which renders *nagid*.

decisions.choice: wakuu wa Wafilisti
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note: the lords of the five Philistine cities are "wakuu wa Wafilisti" at every level.

decisions.choice: "các lãnh chúa Phi-li-tin"
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note for the lords of the five Philistine cities.

source.text: וַיְהִ֞י אַחֲרֵ֣י׀הֵסַ֣בּוּ אֹת֗וֹ וַתְּהִ֨י יַד־יְהוָ֤ה׀בָּעִיר֙ מְהוּמָה֙ גְּדוֹלָ֣ה מְאֹ֔ד וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת־אַנְשֵׁ֣י הָעִ֔יר מִקָּטֹ֖ן וְעַד־גָּד֑וֹל וַיִּשָּׂתְר֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם טְחֹרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was after they had brought it around, and was [the] hand of YHWH against the city — a panic very great — and he struck [the] men of the city from small and to great, and broke out on them tumors.

en.L: And after they had brought it around, the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was against the city [with] a very great panic, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} struck the men of the city, from small to great, and tumors broke out on them.
en.B: But after they had moved it, the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was against that city and threw it into a great panic. He struck the {{gender:people|men}} of the city, young and old, and tumors broke out on them.
en.R: But after the ark came to Gath, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} turned against that city too, and everyone there panicked. He struck the {{gender:people|men}} of the city, young and old, and they broke out in tumors.

es.L: Y después de que la hubieron pasado allá, la mano {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} estuvo contra la ciudad [con] un pánico muy grande, e hirió a los hombres de la ciudad, desde el pequeño hasta el grande, y les brotaron tumores.
es.B: Pero después de trasladarla, la mano {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} se puso contra aquella ciudad y la llenó de un pánico enorme. Hirió a los habitantes de la ciudad, jóvenes y viejos, y les salieron tumores.
es.R: Pero después de que el arca llegó a Gat, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se puso también contra esa ciudad, y todos allí se llenaron de pánico. Hirió a los habitantes de la ciudad, jóvenes y viejos, y les salieron tumores.

fr.L: Et après qu’ils l’eurent fait passer, la main {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} fut contre la ville, [avec] une très grande panique, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} frappa les hommes de la ville, du petit au grand, et des tumeurs éclatèrent sur eux.
fr.B: Mais après qu’on l’eut transportée, la main {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} s’abattit sur la ville et y jeta une très grande panique. Il frappa {{gender:les gens|les hommes}} de la ville, petits et grands, et des tumeurs apparurent sur eux.
fr.R: Mais quand l’arche est arrivée à Gath, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} s’est retourné contre cette ville aussi, et tout le monde a été pris de panique. Il a frappé {{gender:les gens|les hommes}} de la ville, jeunes et vieux, et ils ont eu des tumeurs.

sw.L: Na baada ya kulizungusha, mkono wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ukawa juu ya mji [kwa] hofu kuu sana, akawapiga watu wa mji, tangu mdogo mpaka mkubwa, na majipu yakawatokea.
sw.B: Lakini baada ya kulihamisha, mkono wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ulikuwa dhidi ya mji huo ukautia katika hofu kuu. Akawapiga watu wa mji, wadogo kwa wakubwa, na majipu yakawatokea.
sw.R: Lakini sanduku lilipofika Gathi, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaupiga mji huo pia, na kila mtu huko akaingiwa na hofu kuu. Akawapiga watu wa mji, vijana kwa wazee, na majipu yakawatokea.

vi.L: Sau khi họ đã đem hòm đi vòng qua đó, tay của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nghịch cùng thành ấy [gây ra] một sự hoảng loạn rất lớn; {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đánh người trong thành, từ nhỏ đến lớn, và bướu nổi lên trên họ.
vi.B: Nhưng sau khi họ đã chuyển hòm sang đó, tay của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giáng xuống thành ấy, gây ra sự hoảng loạn rất lớn. Ngài đánh {{gender:dân|đàn ông}} trong thành, cả già lẫn trẻ, và bướu nổi lên trên họ.
vi.R: Nhưng sau khi hòm đến Gát, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cũng trừng phạt thành ấy, và mọi người ở đó đều hoảng loạn. Ngài đánh {{gender:dân|đàn ông}} trong thành, cả già lẫn trẻ, và họ nổi bướu khắp mình.

decisions.choice: the hand of the LORD was against the city with a very great panic
decisions.reason: The words "a very great panic" stand beside the clause without a joining word. They describe the form the LORD's hand took: terror and confusion seized the city.

decisions.choice: from small to great: everyone, young and old
decisions.reason: The phrase covers the whole population, from the least to the greatest, whether by age or by rank.

decisions.choice: broke out: the tumors appeared on their bodies
alternatives: the tumors were in their hidden parts
decisions.reason: The verb is found only here. It is usually understood as "burst out" or "broke out". An older understanding takes it from a similar word meaning "hide", so that the tumors were in their hidden parts.

decisions.choice: tumors: as in verse 6
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, the written form is *'ofalim* and the reading marked by the scribes is *techorim*; see the note there on the uncertain kind of swelling.

decisions.choice: people of the city (default); men of the city (alternative)
decisions.reason: As in verse 7, "men of" the city means its inhabitants, young and old, so Balanced and Readable say "people" by default.

decisions.choice: after the ark came to Gath, the LORD turned against that city too
decisions.reason: Readable names the ark and the city, and says "turned against" for the picture of the LORD's hand being against the city.

source.text: וַֽיְשַׁלְּח֛וּ אֶת־אֲר֥וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים עֶקְר֑וֹן וַיְהִ֗י כְּב֨וֹא אֲר֤וֹן הָאֱלֹהִים֙ עֶקְר֔וֹן וַיִּזְעֲק֨וּ הָֽעֶקְרֹנִ֜ים לֵאמֹ֗ר הֵסַ֤בּוּ אֵלַי֙ אֶת־אֲרוֹן֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לַהֲמִיתֵ֖נִי וְאֶת־עַמִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And they sent the ark of God [to] Ekron; and it was, as came [the] ark of God [to] Ekron, then cried out the Ekronites, saying, they have brought around to me [the] ark of [the] God of Israel to kill me and my people.

en.L: And they sent the ark of God to Ekron. And as the ark of God came to Ekron, the Ekronites cried out, saying, "They have brought the ark of the God of Israel around to me, to kill me and my people!"
en.B: So they sent the ark of God on to Ekron. But as soon as the ark of God arrived in Ekron, the people of Ekron cried out, "They have brought the ark of the God of Israel over to us to kill us and our people!"
en.R: Then they sent the ark of God to Ekron. As soon as it arrived, the people of Ekron shouted, "They have brought the ark of Israel's God here to kill us and our people!"

es.L: Y enviaron el arca de Dios a Ecrón. Y cuando el arca de Dios llegó a Ecrón, los de Ecrón gritaron diciendo: «¡Me han traído el arca del Dios de Israel para matarme a mí y a mi pueblo!».
es.B: Entonces enviaron el arca de Dios a Ecrón. Pero en cuanto el arca de Dios llegó a Ecrón, los habitantes de Ecrón gritaron: «¡Nos han traído el arca del Dios de Israel para matarnos a nosotros y a nuestra gente!».
es.R: Luego enviaron el arca de Dios a Ecrón. En cuanto llegó, los habitantes de Ecrón gritaron: «¡Han traído aquí el arca del Dios de Israel para matarnos a nosotros y a nuestra gente!».

fr.L: Et ils envoyèrent l’arche de Dieu à Eqrôn. Et quand l’arche de Dieu arriva à Eqrôn, les Eqronites poussèrent des cris, en disant : « Ils m’ont fait passer l’arche du Dieu d’Israël pour me faire mourir, moi et mon peuple ! »
fr.B: On envoya donc l’arche de Dieu à Eqrôn. Mais dès que l’arche de Dieu arriva à Eqrôn, les habitants d’Eqrôn s’écrièrent : « On nous a amené l’arche du Dieu d’Israël pour nous faire mourir, nous et notre peuple ! »
fr.R: Ensuite, ils ont envoyé l’arche de Dieu à Eqrôn. Dès qu’elle est arrivée, les habitants d’Eqrôn ont crié : « Ils ont amené ici l’arche du Dieu d’Israël pour nous tuer, nous et notre peuple ! »

sw.L: Nao wakalipeleka sanduku la Mungu Ekroni. Na sanduku la Mungu lilipofika Ekroni, Waekroni wakapiga kelele wakisema, "Wamenizungushia sanduku la Mungu wa Israeli ili kuniua mimi na watu wangu!"
sw.B: Basi wakalipeleka sanduku la Mungu Ekroni. Lakini mara tu sanduku la Mungu lilipofika Ekroni, watu wa Ekroni wakalia kwa sauti, "Wametuletea sanduku la Mungu wa Israeli ili kutuua sisi na watu wetu!"
sw.R: Kisha wakalipeleka sanduku la Mungu Ekroni. Mara tu lilipofika, watu wa Ekroni wakapiga kelele, "Wametuletea hapa sanduku la Mungu wa Israeli ili kutuua sisi na watu wetu!"

vi.L: Họ gửi hòm của Đức Chúa Trời đến Éc-rôn. Khi hòm của Đức Chúa Trời vừa đến Éc-rôn, người Éc-rôn kêu la rằng: "Họ đã đem hòm của Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên vòng qua tôi để giết tôi và dân tôi!"
vi.B: Vậy họ gửi hòm của Đức Chúa Trời đến Éc-rôn. Nhưng hòm của Đức Chúa Trời vừa đến Éc-rôn thì dân Éc-rôn kêu la: "Họ đem hòm của Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên đến đây để giết chúng ta và dân chúng ta!"
vi.R: Rồi họ gửi hòm của Đức Chúa Trời đến Éc-rôn. Hòm vừa đến nơi, dân Éc-rôn la lên: "Họ đem hòm của Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên đến đây để giết chúng ta và dân chúng ta!"

decisions.choice: Ekron: the Philistine city nearest Israel's land
decisions.reason: Ekron lay to the north, on the border of the territory given to Judah (Joshua 15:11). From there the ark would be sent home (6:16).

decisions.choice: me and my people: the city speaks as one
decisions.reason: The Ekronites cry out in the singular, "to me ... to kill me and my people". Each speaks for himself and his people, or the city speaks as one voice.

decisions.choice: they have brought it to kill us: the Ekronites already know what the ark brings
decisions.reason: They do not wait for the disease to arrive. News of Ashdod and Gath has gone before the ark, and they blame those who sent it.

decisions.choice: us, our people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plural for a crowd speaking together; Literal keeps the singular of the Hebrew.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלְח֨וּ וַיַּאַסְפ֜וּ אֶת־כָּל־סַרְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ שַׁלְּח֞וּ אֶת־אֲר֨וֹן אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְיָשֹׁ֣ב לִמְקֹמ֔וֹ וְלֹֽא־יָמִ֥ית אֹתִ֖י וְאֶת־עַמִּ֑י כִּֽי־הָיְתָ֤ה מְהֽוּמַת־מָ֨וֶת֙ בְּכָל־הָעִ֔יר כָּבְדָ֥ה מְאֹ֛ד יַ֥ד הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they sent and gathered all [the] rulers of [the] Philistines, and said, send away [the] ark of [the] God of Israel, and let it return to its place, and not will it kill me and my people; for there was a panic of death in all the city; heavy very [was the] hand of God there.

en.L: And they sent and gathered all the rulers of the Philistines, and said, "Send away the ark of the God of Israel, and let it return to its place, so that it does not kill me and my people." For there was a panic of death in all the city; the hand of God was very heavy there.
en.B: So they sent for all the rulers of the Philistines and gathered them together. "Send the ark of the God of Israel away," they said. "Let it go back to its own place, so that it does not kill us and our people." For a deadly panic had spread through the whole city; the hand of God was very heavy there.
en.R: So they called together all the rulers of the Philistines again. "Send the ark of the God of Israel away!" they said. "Let it go back where it belongs, or it will kill us and our people." The whole city was full of panic and death, because God was dealing very harshly with the people there.

es.L: Y enviaron a reunir a todos los jefes de los filisteos, y dijeron: «{{plural_you:Despidan|Despedid}} el arca del Dios de Israel, y que vuelva a su lugar, para que no me mate a mí y a mi pueblo». Porque había un pánico de muerte en toda la ciudad; la mano de Dios era muy pesada allí.
es.B: Así que mandaron llamar a todos los jefes de los filisteos y los reunieron. «{{plural_you:Devuelvan|Devolved}} el arca del Dios de Israel», dijeron. «Que vuelva a su lugar, para que no nos mate a nosotros y a nuestra gente». Porque un pánico mortal se había extendido por toda la ciudad; la mano de Dios pesaba mucho allí.
es.R: Entonces volvieron a reunir a todos los jefes de los filisteos. «¡{{plural_you:Devuelvan|Devolved}} el arca del Dios de Israel!», dijeron. «Que vuelva a su lugar, o nos matará a nosotros y a nuestra gente». Toda la ciudad estaba llena de pánico y de muerte, porque Dios estaba castigando con mucha dureza a la gente de allí.

fr.L: Et ils envoyèrent rassembler tous les princes des Philistins, et dirent : « Renvoyez l’arche du Dieu d’Israël, et qu’elle retourne à sa place, et qu’elle ne me fasse pas mourir, moi et mon peuple. » Car il y avait une panique mortelle dans toute la ville ; la main de Dieu y était très lourde.
fr.B: Ils firent donc venir tous les princes des Philistins et les réunirent. « Renvoyez l’arche du Dieu d’Israël, dirent-ils. Qu’elle retourne chez elle, pour qu’elle ne nous fasse pas mourir, nous et notre peuple. » Car une panique mortelle s’était répandue dans toute la ville ; la main de Dieu y pesait très lourdement.
fr.R: Alors ils ont de nouveau réuni tous les princes des Philistins. « Renvoyez l’arche du Dieu d’Israël ! ont-ils dit. Qu’elle retourne chez elle, sinon elle va nous tuer, nous et notre peuple. » Toute la ville était pleine de panique et de morts, parce que Dieu traitait très durement les gens de cette ville.

sw.L: Nao wakatuma wakawakusanya wakuu wote wa Wafilisti, wakasema, "Lipelekeni mbali sanduku la Mungu wa Israeli, lirudi mahali pake, lisije likaniua mimi na watu wangu." Kwa maana palikuwa na hofu ya kifo katika mji wote; mkono wa Mungu ulikuwa mzito sana huko.
sw.B: Basi wakatuma ujumbe wakawakusanya wakuu wote wa Wafilisti. Wakasema, "Lipelekeni mbali sanduku la Mungu wa Israeli. Lirudi mahali pake, lisije likatuua sisi na watu wetu." Kwa maana hofu ya kifo ilikuwa imeenea mji wote; mkono wa Mungu ulikuwa mzito sana huko.
sw.R: Basi wakawaita tena wakuu wote wa Wafilisti wakutane. Wakasema, "Lipelekeni mbali sanduku la Mungu wa Israeli! Lirudi mahali pake, la sivyo litatuua sisi na watu wetu." Mji wote ulijaa hofu na vifo, kwa sababu Mungu alikuwa akiwatendea watu wa huko kwa ukali mwingi.

vi.L: Họ sai người đi triệu tập tất cả các lãnh chúa Phi-li-tin và nói: "Hãy gửi hòm của Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên đi, để nó trở về chỗ của nó, kẻo nó giết tôi và dân tôi." Vì có sự hoảng loạn chết chóc trong khắp thành; tay của Đức Chúa Trời đè rất nặng tại đó.
vi.B: Vậy họ sai người mời tất cả các lãnh chúa Phi-li-tin họp lại và nói: "Hãy gửi hòm của Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên đi. Hãy để hòm trở về chỗ cũ, kẻo hòm giết chúng ta và dân chúng ta." Vì sự hoảng loạn chết chóc đã lan khắp thành; tay của Đức Chúa Trời đè rất nặng trên nơi đó.
vi.R: Vậy họ lại mời tất cả các lãnh chúa Phi-li-tin đến họp. Họ nói: "Hãy gửi hòm của Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên đi! Hãy để hòm trở về nơi của nó, kẻo hòm giết chúng ta và dân chúng ta." Cả thành đầy hoảng loạn và chết chóc, vì Đức Chúa Trời trừng phạt dân ở đó rất nặng.

decisions.choice: a panic of death: deadly panic
decisions.reason: The panic of verse 9 has now become a panic with death in it: people were dying, and the rest were terrified that they would be next (verse 12).

decisions.choice: the hand of God was very heavy there: the heavy hand that began in verse 6
decisions.reason: The "heavy hand" closes the story of the ark's journey through Philistia (verses 6, 7, 9). The word "heavy" belongs to the same family as the word "glory": Ichabod's name said that the glory had gone from Israel (4:21-22), yet God's weight now presses on the land that took the ark.

decisions.choice: let it return ... so that it does not kill: the purpose of sending it away
decisions.reason: The requests are linked: send it home, so that it will stop killing. As in verse 10 the people speak in the singular, "me and my people".

decisions.choice: us, our people
decisions.reason: As in verse 10, Balanced and Readable use the plural for the crowd.

decisions.choice: again; God was dealing very harshly with the people
decisions.reason: Readable adds "again" because the rulers were called a second time (verse 8), and explains the heavy hand as in verse 6.

source.text: וְהָֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־מֵ֔תוּ הֻכּ֖וּ בַּטְּחֹרִ֑יםוַתַּ֛עַל שַֽׁוְעַ֥ת הָעִ֖יר הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And the men who not died were struck with tumors, and went up [the] cry of the city [to] the heavens.

en.L: And the men who did not die were struck with tumors, and the cry of the city went up to the heavens.
en.B: Those who did not die were struck with tumors, and the cry of the city for help rose up to heaven.
en.R: Those who did not die had tumors. The people of the city cried out for help, and their cry went up to heaven.

es.L: Y los hombres que no murieron fueron heridos con tumores, y el clamor de la ciudad subió a los cielos.
es.B: Los que no murieron fueron heridos con tumores, y el clamor de la ciudad subió hasta el cielo.
es.R: Los que no murieron tenían tumores. La gente de la ciudad pedía ayuda a gritos, y su clamor subía hasta el cielo.

fr.L: Et les hommes qui ne moururent pas furent frappés de tumeurs, et le cri de la ville monta jusqu’aux cieux.
fr.B: Ceux qui ne moururent pas furent frappés de tumeurs, et le cri de détresse de la ville monta jusqu’au ciel.
fr.R: Ceux qui ne sont pas morts ont eu des tumeurs. Les habitants de la ville ont crié au secours, et leur cri est monté jusqu’au ciel.

sw.L: Na watu wasiokufa walipigwa kwa majipu, na kilio cha mji kikapanda mpaka mbinguni.
sw.B: Wale ambao hawakufa walipigwa kwa majipu, na kilio cha mji cha kuomba msaada kikapanda mpaka mbinguni.
sw.R: Wale ambao hawakufa walikuwa na majipu. Watu wa mji walilia wakiomba msaada, na kilio chao kikapanda mpaka mbinguni.

vi.L: Những người không chết thì bị đánh bằng bướu, và tiếng kêu la của thành vọng lên đến các tầng trời.
vi.B: Những người không chết thì bị nổi bướu, và tiếng kêu cứu của thành vọng lên tận trời.
vi.R: Những người không chết thì bị nổi bướu. Dân thành kêu cứu, và tiếng kêu của họ vọng lên tận trời.

decisions.choice: the cry of the city: a cry for help in distress
decisions.reason: The word is used for a desperate call for rescue. It recalls Israel in Egypt, whose cry for help went up to God (Exodus 2:23), but now it is the Philistines who cry out.

decisions.choice: tumors: as in verse 6
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, the written form is *'ofalim* and the reading marked by the scribes is *techorim*.

decisions.choice: went up to the heavens: a loud and desperate cry
decisions.reason: The cry rose high into the sky, so loud and so great was the distress.

decisions.choice: Those who
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the men", meaning the people of the city who survived, so Balanced and Readable say "those", which includes everyone.
